title: Round 4 / ECDLP-12: relation yield of small-x factor bases on prime-field curves
question: Measure, at toy sizes, decomposition probabilities and relation-collection cost for small-x factor bases on E(F_p) (m = 2, 3), compared with sqrt(p) and heuristic predictions.
claims: EMPIRICAL (12 prime-order toy curves, p in ~[3.8e3,2.8e5], exact enumeration): decomposition probability pi(m,B) over m-sums of V_B matches n^m/(m! r) with n=|V_B| (both signs) within 0-30% (below it as pi saturates); the sign-doubled (2n)^m/(m! r) overestimates ~2^m at small pi.

EMPIRICAL (unit-cost model, toy sizes only): no tested (m in {2,3}, beta in {0.5,1,2}) relation-collection plus linear-algebra cost falls below sqrt(p); minimum ratio to sqrt(p) at 2^18 is 15.7 (m=3, beta=0.5); hypothesis HYP-db508348 SURVIVES on the tested domain only, no asymptotic claim.

S_3 for short Weierstrass verified against the group law (0 failures in ~8000 checks) and the Semaev m=2 route agrees with brute force on 600/600 random R; it is cheaper than the (m-1)-table naive route but not than the full m-sum table.
End-to-end toy index calculus recovered k correctly (verified by k*P==Q and dlog_bsgs) at p=4001 and p=15791 at 40-52x sqrt(p) measured units.
next_action: PI review of cost-model assumptions (unit weights, sign-symmetry favour, epsilon); optionally explore beta>2, m>=4 and weighted field-op costs; independent replication with a second seed.
